subject: Geography
central_question: How do India’s transport and communication networks move people, goods, information and ideas, and how do their forms and spatial patterns support national integration and economic development?
in_scope_units: Meaning and major modes of transport and communication
Road transport and classification of roads
National Highways, NHAI, Golden Quadrilateral, corridors, Bharatmala and Border Roads
Rail transport, zones, gauges, modernisation, metro systems and Konkan Railway
Water transport, inland waterways and oceanic routes
Air transport, Airport Authority of India, UDAN and Pawan Hans
Mass communication through radio and television
Satellite communication through INSAT, IRS, PSLV and NRSC
banned_topics: Detailed composition of exports and imports, which belongs to International Trade
Detailed mineral and petroleum distribution, which belongs to Mineral and Energy Resources

known_pitfalls.claim: Transport and communication perform the same function.
known_pitfalls.correction: Transport moves people and material goods, while communication moves ideas, views, messages and information.

known_pitfalls.claim: National Highways form most of India’s road length.
known_pitfalls.correction: They form a small share of total road length but carry a large share of road traffic.

known_pitfalls.claim: Water transport is the fastest mode.
known_pitfalls.correction: Air transport is the fastest; waterways are valued for low cost, fuel efficiency and heavy, bulky cargo.

known_pitfalls.claim: Satellites are used only for television.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter includes telecommunications, weather observation, disaster monitoring, border surveillance and natural-resource management.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 2(i) to define transportation and name its major modes.
Use NCERT Exercise 1(i) to recall the number of railway zones stated in the chapter.
Use NCERT Exercise 1(ii) to identify National Waterway No. 1.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(iii) to define communication.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(ii) to write a connected account of railway development and importance.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1–3 and a PROJECT: three MCQs, three short-answer questions, three long-answer questions and one railway-passenger-facilities project.
